content: Homage to that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Fully Awakened Buddha[By this mark the question of our own school is shown] Is a person found as a real and ultimate fact [variant: saccikaṭṭhaparamaṭṭhenāti (Syā., Pī., Ka., Sī.)]? Yes. Is the person found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as a real fact, an ultimate fact, is found? That should not be said.Acknowledge the refutation. If a person is found as a real and ultimate fact, then surely you must also say: "The person is found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as a real fact, an ultimate fact, is found." What you say here — that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact" should be said but "the person is found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as a real fact, an ultimate fact, is found" should not be said — is wrong.But if "the person is found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as a real fact, an ultimate fact, is found" should not be said, then surely [variant: no vata re (Syā., Pī.)] "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact" should not be said either. What you say here — that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact" should be said but "the person is found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as a real fact, an ultimate fact, is found" should not be said — is wrong.The forward set of five.[By this mark the question of the other school is shown] Is a person not found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. Is the person not found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as a real fact, an ultimate fact, is found? That should not be said.Acknowledge the counter-refutation. If a person is not found as a real and ultimate fact, then surely you must also say: "The person is not found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as a real fact, an ultimate fact, is found." What you say here — that "a person is not found as a real and ultimate fact" should be said but "the person is not found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as a real fact, an ultimate fact, is found" should not be said — is wrong.But if "the person is not found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as a real fact, an ultimate fact, is found" should not be said, then surely "a person is not found as a real and ultimate fact" should not be said either. What you say here — that "a person is not found as a real and ultimate fact" should be said but "the person is not found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as a real fact, an ultimate fact, is found" should not be said — is wrong.The counter-refutation set of four.But if you think that "a person is not found as a real and ultimate fact" should be said but "the person is not found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as a real fact, an ultimate fact, is found" should not be said, then on the grounds of that assertion of yours [variant: tvaṃ (Syā.); the sub-commentary should be consulted], you, admitting this [the sub-commentary should be consulted], must be refuted in this way. So we refute you, and you are rightly refuted [variant: suniggahitova (Syā.)].If a person is not found as a real and ultimate fact, then surely you must also say: "The person is not found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as a real fact, an ultimate fact, is found." But isn't it the case that an arahant neither abandons nor clings, but is established having abandoned; neither scatters nor binds, but is established having scattered; isn't it the case that an arahant neither puts out nor kindles, but is established having put out? Yes. If an arahant neither puts out nor kindles, but is established having put out, then surely you must not say: "An arahant attains final nibbāna with wholesome consciousness."Should it not be said that "an arahant attains final nibbāna with wholesome consciousness"? Yes. But isn't it the case that an arahant attains final nibbāna with mindfulness established, mindful and clearly comprehending? Yes. If an arahant attains final nibbāna with mindfulness established, mindful and clearly comprehending, then surely you must also say: "An arahant attains final nibbāna with wholesome consciousness."The Discussion of Wholesome Consciousness is complete.Does an arahant attain final nibbāna while established in the imperturbable? Yes. But isn't it the case that an arahant attains final nibbāna while established in the ordinary mind? Yes. If an arahant attains final nibbāna while established in the ordinary mind, then surely you must not say: "An arahant attains final nibbāna while established in the imperturbable."Does an arahant attain final nibbāna while established in the imperturbable? Yes. Does an arahant attain final nibbāna while established in functional consciousness? That should not be said… But isn't it the case that an arahant attains final nibbāna while established in consciousness that is a result? Yes. If an arahant attains final nibbāna while established in consciousness that is a result, then surely you must not say: "An arahant attains final nibbāna while established in the imperturbable."Does an arahant attain final nibbāna while established in the imperturbable? Yes. Does an arahant attain final nibbāna while established in consciousness that is functional and indeterminate? That should not be said… But isn't it the case that an arahant attains final nibbāna while established in consciousness that is a result and indeterminate? Yes. If an arahant attains final nibbāna while established in consciousness that is a result and indeterminate, then surely you must not say: "An arahant attains final nibbāna while established in the imperturbable."Does an arahant attain final nibbāna while established in the imperturbable? Yes. But isn't it the case that the Blessed One, after emerging from the fourth jhāna, attained final nibbāna immediately afterwards [Dī. Ni. 2.219]? Yes. If the Blessed One, after emerging from the fourth jhāna, attained final nibbāna immediately afterwards, then surely you must not say: "An arahant attains final nibbāna while established in the imperturbable."The Discussion of the Imperturbable is complete.Is there a breakthrough to the Dhamma for one lying in the womb? Yes. For one lying in the womb, is there teaching of the Dhamma, listening to the Dhamma, discussion of the Dhamma, questioning, undertaking of virtue, guarding the doors of the senses, moderation in eating, and devotion to wakefulness in the first and last parts of the night? That should not be said… For one lying in the womb, is there no teaching of the Dhamma, no listening to the Dhamma … no devotion to wakefulness in the first and last parts of the night? Yes. If, for one lying in the womb, there is no teaching of the Dhamma, no listening to the Dhamma … no devotion to wakefulness in the first and last parts of the night, then surely you must not say: "There is a breakthrough to the Dhamma for one lying in the womb."Is there a breakthrough to the Dhamma for one lying in the womb? Yes. But isn't it the case that there are two conditions for the arising of right view: the voice of another, and wise attention? Yes. If there are two conditions for the arising of right view: the voice of another, and wise attention, then surely you must not say: "There is a breakthrough to the Dhamma for one lying in the womb."Is there a breakthrough to the Dhamma for one lying in the womb? Yes. Is there a breakthrough to the Dhamma for one who is asleep, heedless, unmindful and not clearly comprehending? That should not be said…The Discussion of the Breakthrough to the Dhamma is complete.Is there attainment of arahantship for one lying in the womb? Yes. Is there attainment of arahantship for one who is asleep, heedless, unmindful and not clearly comprehending? That should not be said…Is there a breakthrough to the Dhamma for one who is dreaming? Yes. Is there a breakthrough to the Dhamma for one who is asleep, heedless, unmindful and not clearly comprehending? That should not be said…Is there attainment of arahantship for one who is dreaming? Yes. Is there attainment of arahantship for one who is asleep, heedless, unmindful and not clearly comprehending? That should not be said…The Discussion of All Three is complete.Is all the consciousness of one who is dreaming indeterminate? Yes. Could one kill a living being in a dream? Yes. If one could kill a living being in a dream, then surely you must not say: "All the consciousness of one who is dreaming is indeterminate."Could one in a dream take what is not given … speak falsely, speak divisively, speak harshly, chatter idly, break into houses, carry off plunder, rob a single house, lie in ambush, go to another's wife, plunder a village, plunder a town; could one in a dream engage in sexual intercourse; could impure fluid be emitted from one who is dreaming; could one in a dream give a gift, give a robe, give almsfood, give lodging, give medicine and requisites for the sick, give food, give meals, give drink, pay homage to a shrine, offer garlands at a shrine, offer scents, offer ointment … walk around a shrine keeping it on the right? Yes. If one could in a dream walk around a shrine keeping it on the right, then surely you must not say: "All the consciousness of one who is dreaming is indeterminate."Should it not be said that "all the consciousness of one who is dreaming is indeterminate"? Yes. But isn't it the case that the Blessed One declared the consciousness of one who is dreaming to be of no account? Yes. If the Blessed One declared the consciousness of one who is dreaming to be of no account, then surely you must also say: "All the consciousness of one who is dreaming is indeterminate."The Discussion of the Indeterminate is complete.Is there no repetition condition at all? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, killing living beings, when pursued, developed and cultivated, leads to hell, leads to the animal realm, leads to the realm of ghosts; the lightest result of killing living beings, for one who becomes a human, leads to a short life" [A. Ni. 8.40]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case, there is a repetition condition.Is there no repetition condition at all? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, taking what is not given, when pursued, developed and cultivated, leads to hell, leads to the animal realm, leads to the realm of ghosts; the lightest result of taking what is not given, for one who becomes a human, leads to loss of wealth … the lightest result of sexual misconduct, for one who becomes a human, leads to rivalry and enmity … the lightest result of false speech, for one who becomes a human, leads to being falsely accused … the lightest result of divisive speech, for one who becomes a human, leads to being split from friends … the lightest result of harsh speech, for one who becomes a human, leads to hearing unpleasant sounds … the lightest result of idle chatter, for one who becomes a human, leads to speech that is not accepted; monks, drinking liquor and wine, when pursued … the lightest result of drinking liquor and wine, for one who becomes a human, leads to madness" [A. Ni. 8.40]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case, there is a repetition condition.Is there no repetition condition at all? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, wrong view, when pursued, developed and cultivated, leads to hell, leads to the animal realm, leads to the realm of ghosts"? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case, there is a repetition condition.Is there no repetition condition at all? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, wrong intention … wrong concentration, when pursued, developed … leads to the realm of ghosts"? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case, there is a repetition condition.Is there no repetition condition at all? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, right view, when pursued, developed and cultivated, merges into the deathless, has the deathless as its final resort, has the deathless as its culmination"? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case, there is a repetition condition.Is there no repetition condition at all? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, right intention, when pursued, developed and cultivated … monks, right concentration, when pursued, developed and cultivated, merges into the deathless, has the deathless as its final resort, has the deathless as its culmination"? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case, there is a repetition condition.The Discussion of the Repetition Condition is complete.Do all phenomena last for a single moment of consciousness? Yes. Does the great earth last for just one moment of consciousness, does the great ocean stay, does Sineru, the king of mountains, stay, does water stay, does fire stay, does air stay, do grass, wood and forest trees last for just one moment of consciousness? That should not be said…Do all phenomena last for a single moment of consciousness? Yes. Is the eye base co-arising with eye-consciousness? That should not be said… Is the eye base co-arising with eye-consciousness? Yes. But did venerable Sāriputta not say this: "Friends, if the internal eye is intact but external visible forms do not come into its range, and there is no corresponding bringing to mind, then there is no manifestation of the corresponding section of consciousness [variant: viññāṇabhāvassa (many editions)]. Friends, if the internal eye is intact and external visible forms come into its range, but there is no corresponding bringing to mind, then there is no manifestation of the corresponding section of consciousness. But when, friends, the internal eye is intact, external visible forms come into its range, and there is the corresponding bringing to mind, then there is the manifestation of the corresponding section of consciousness" [Ma. Ni. 1.306]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "the eye base is co-arising with eye-consciousness."Is the ear base … the nose base … the tongue base … the body base co-arising with body-consciousness? That should not be said… Is the body base co-arising with body-consciousness? Yes. But did venerable Sāriputta not say this: "Friends, if the internal body is intact but external tangibles do not come into its range, and there is no … Friends, if the internal body is intact and external tangibles come into its range, but there is no … But when, friends, the internal body is intact, external tangibles come into its range, and there is the corresponding bringing to mind, then there is the manifestation of the corresponding section of consciousness" [Ma. Ni. 1.306]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "the body base is co-arising with body-consciousness."Should it not be said that "all phenomena last for a single moment of consciousness"? Yes. Are all phenomena permanent, stable, eternal, not subject to change? That should not be said. In that case, all phenomena last for a single moment of consciousness.The Discussion of the Momentary is complete.The Twenty-Second Chapter.Its summary:There is final nibbāna without abandoning some fetter; an arahant attains final nibbāna with wholesome consciousness; an arahant attains final nibbāna while established in the imperturbable; there is a breakthrough to the Dhamma for one lying in the womb; there is attainment of arahantship for one lying in the womb; there is a breakthrough to the Dhamma for one who is dreaming; there is attainment of arahantship for one who is dreaming; all the consciousness of one who is dreaming is indeterminate; there is no repetition condition at all; all phenomena last for a single moment of consciousness.May sexual intercourse be engaged in with a shared intention? Yes. With a shared intention, does one become a non-ascetic, become a non-monk, become one whose root is cut, become one who has incurred defeat (an offence entailing expulsion)? That should not be said… May sexual intercourse be engaged in with a shared intention? Yes. With a shared intention, may a living being be killed, what is not given be taken, a falsehood be spoken, divisive words be spoken, harsh words be spoken, idle chatter be engaged in, houses be broken into, plunder be carried off, a single house be robbed, an ambush be laid, another's wife be gone to, a village be plundered, a town be plundered? That should not be said…The Discussion of Shared Intention is complete.Do non-human beings engage in sexual intercourse in the appearance of arahants? Yes. Do non-human beings, in the appearance of arahants, kill living beings … take what is not given, speak falsely, speak divisively, speak harshly, chatter idly, break into houses, carry off plunder, rob single houses, lie in ambush, go to others' wives, plunder villages … plunder towns? That should not be said…The Discussion of the Appearance of Arahants is complete.Does the bodhisatta go to the lower world by acting at will through his own sovereignty? Yes. Does the bodhisatta, by acting at will through his own sovereignty, go to hell, go to the Sañjīva hell, go to the Kālasutta hell, go to the Tāpana hell, go to the Mahātāpana hell [variant: patāpanaṃ (Sī., Syā., Kaṃ., Pī.)], go to the Saṅghātaka hell, go to the Roruva hell … go to the Avīci hell? That should not be said…Does the bodhisatta go to the lower world by acting at will through his own sovereignty? Yes. "The bodhisatta goes to the lower world by acting at will through his own sovereignty" — is there really such a discourse? There is not. If there is no such discourse: "The bodhisatta goes to the lower world by acting at will through his own sovereignty," then surely you must not say: "The bodhisatta goes to the lower world by acting at will through his own sovereignty."Does the bodhisatta descend into a womb by acting at will through his own sovereignty? Yes. Could the bodhisatta, by acting at will through his own sovereignty, be reborn in hell, be reborn in the animal realm? That should not be said…Does the bodhisatta descend into a womb by acting at will through his own sovereignty? Yes. Does the bodhisatta have psychic power? That should not be said… Does the bodhisatta have psychic power? Yes. Has the bodhisatta cultivated the base of psychic power consisting of desire … the base of psychic power consisting of energy … the base of psychic power consisting of mind … the base of psychic power consisting of investigation? That should not be said…Does the bodhisatta descend into a womb by acting at will through his own sovereignty? Yes. "The bodhisatta descends into a womb by acting at will through his own sovereignty" — is there really such a discourse? There is not. If there is no such discourse: "The bodhisatta descends into a womb by acting at will through his own sovereignty," then surely you must not say: "The bodhisatta descends into a womb by acting at will through his own sovereignty."Did the bodhisatta practise severe austerities by acting at will through his own sovereignty? Yes. Did the bodhisatta, by acting at will through his own sovereignty, adopt the view "the world is eternal," "the world is not eternal" … "the world is finite" … "the world is infinite" … "the soul is the same as the body" … "the soul is one thing, the body another" … "the Tathāgata (the Buddha) exists after death" … "the Tathāgata does not exist after death" … "the Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death" … adopt the view "the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death"? That should not be said…Did the bodhisatta practise severe austerities by acting at will through his own sovereignty? Yes. "The bodhisatta practised severe austerities by acting at will through his own sovereignty" — is there really such a discourse? There is not. If there is no such discourse: "The bodhisatta practised severe austerities by acting at will through his own sovereignty," then surely you must not say: "The bodhisatta practised severe austerities by acting at will through his own sovereignty."Did the bodhisatta, by acting at will through his own sovereignty, practise another kind of austerity [variant: amaraṃ tapaṃ (Saṃ. Ni. 1.137)] and acknowledge another teacher? Yes. Did the bodhisatta, by acting at will through his own sovereignty, adopt the view "the world is eternal" … adopt the view "the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death"? That should not be said…Did the bodhisatta acknowledge another teacher by acting at will through his own sovereignty? Yes. "The bodhisatta acknowledged another teacher by acting at will through his own sovereignty" — is there really such a discourse? There is not. If there is no such discourse: "The bodhisatta acknowledged another teacher by acting at will through his own sovereignty," then surely you must not say: "The bodhisatta acknowledged another teacher by acting at will through his own sovereignty."The Discussion of Acting at Will through Sovereignty is complete.Is there something that is not lust but resembles lust? Yes. Is there something that is not contact but resembles contact, something that is not feeling but resembles feeling, something that is not perception but resembles perception, something that is not volition but resembles volition, something that is not consciousness but resembles consciousness, something that is not faith but resembles faith, something that is not energy but resembles energy, something that is not mindfulness but resembles mindfulness, something that is not concentration but resembles concentration, something that is not wisdom but resembles wisdom? That should not be said…Is there something that is not hatred but resembles hatred, something that is not delusion but resembles delusion, something that is not a defilement but resembles a defilement? Yes. Is there something that is not contact but resembles contact … something that is not wisdom but resembles wisdom? That should not be said…The Discussion of Counterfeits is complete.Is material form not concretely produced? Yes. Is material form not impermanent, not conditioned, not dependently arisen, not subject to destruction, not subject to passing, not subject to fading, not subject to cessation, not subject to change? That should not be said… But isn't it the case that material form is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to passing, subject to fading, subject to cessation, subject to change? Yes. If material form is impermanent, conditioned … subject to change, then surely you must not say: "Material form is not concretely produced."Is only suffering concretely produced? Yes. But isn't it the case that the Blessed One declared that what is impermanent is suffering [Saṃ. Ni. 3.15], and declared: "Material form is impermanent"? Yes. If the Blessed One declared that what is impermanent is suffering, and declared: "Material form is impermanent," then surely you must not say: "Only suffering is concretely produced." …Is feeling … perception … are formations … is consciousness … the eye base … the mind-object base … the eye element … the element of mental objects … the eye faculty … the faculty of one who has fully known not concretely produced? Yes. Is the faculty of one who has fully known not impermanent … not subject to change? That should not be said… But isn't it the case that the faculty of one who has fully known is impermanent, conditioned … subject to change? Yes. If the faculty of one who has fully known is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to passing, subject to fading, subject to cessation, subject to change, then surely you must not say: "The faculty of one who has fully known is not concretely produced."Is only suffering concretely produced? Yes. But isn't it the case that the Blessed One declared that what is impermanent is suffering, and declared: "The faculty of one who has fully known is impermanent"? Yes. If the Blessed One declared that what is impermanent is suffering, and declared: "The faculty of one who has fully known is impermanent," then surely you must not say: "Only suffering is concretely produced."The Discussion of the Not Concretely Produced is complete.The Twenty-Third Chapter.Its summary:Sexual intercourse may be engaged in with a shared intention; non-human beings engage in sexual intercourse in the appearance of arahants; the bodhisatta goes to the lower world by acting at will through his own sovereignty, descends into a womb, practised severe austerities, practised another kind of austerity, acknowledged another teacher; there is something that is not lust but resembles lust, something that is not hatred but resembles hatred, something that is not delusion but resembles delusion, something that is not a defilement but resembles a defilement; material form is not concretely produced, the faculty of one who has fully known is not concretely produced.The Small Half-Set.Its summary:Made new, final nibbāna, shared intention.Summary of the sets of fifty:The Great, the fixed course, the underlying tendencies, restraining, and the small one as the fifth;crushing the doctrines of others, well grounded in the root of the discourses;illuminating the Teacher's doctrine, in the treatise Points of Discussion.Thirty-five recitation sections.The treatise Points of Discussion is complete.
